reasons: No test file was shown for this file.
Two label sets overlap, honesty labels here and verification labels in types.ts, and are easy to mix up.
The file does not show whether results from the newer v3 engine are checked against it.

terms.meaning: a written rule describing the exact shape a piece of data must have.
a library that checks data against schemas and reports what does not match.
a label showing how well a fact was checked against its source.
the code that builds the PowerPoint file from the result.
the file format used by Microsoft PowerPoint.
the first version of this result contract, used by the older engines.
a standard framing slide, such as the cover or the agenda, that every deck starts with.

sections.name: File setup, OUTCOMES, Outcome
sections.title: Imports and outcome names
sections.what: Brings in the validation library and two shared research contract rules. Lists the five allowed project outcomes, including Unassessed.
sections.why: The header says this file is the single contract the renderer reads, so the outcome names are fixed here.
sections.watch_out: The newer types file lists only four outcomes, so a project marked Unassessed here may break code that expects four.

sections.name: honestyBadgeSchema
sections.title: Honesty badge labels
sections.what: Lists the six labels that show how well a fact was checked, such as verified, partial, unconfirmed, unreachable, unsourced and held out.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list keeps the wording shown in the report consistent.
sections.watch_out: The unconfirmed label here plays the same role as unverified in the newer types file, so keep the two in step when mapping old data.

sections.name: factSchema
sections.title: Fact rules
sections.what: Describes one saved fact: its text, source, publisher, the field it came from, the pillar it supports, its relevance, and optional markers for how it was classified.
sections.why: Likely reason: the slides need these fields to cite each statement.
sections.watch_out: The evidence kind marker is absent on older runs, so code that reads it must allow it to be missing.

sections.name: projectOutcomeSchema
sections.title: Project outcome rules
sections.what: Describes one project's saved outcome: name, industry, country, status, outcome label, planned and actual budgets, cost overrun percentage, delay in months and technology.
sections.why: Likely reason: the slides show these values for each project, so they are stored as plain numbers.
sections.watch_out: Budget fields are named in millions, so values in other units must be converted before they are saved here.

sections.name: subDriverSchema
sections.title: Sub-driver rules
sections.what: Describes one sub-driver: its text, rationale, the facts it rests on, how many supporting and risk facts it has, and optional markers showing how it was named and whether it is generic.
sections.why: The optional markers were added later, so older results without them still load.
sections.watch_out: The name source can be model_rejected_fallback, meaning the model's name was refused and a standard one was used instead.

sections.name: pillarSchema
sections.title: Pillar rules
sections.what: Describes one pillar: its sub-drivers, its facts, the count of projects on each side, the basis its drivers were built from, and the methodology support quotes.
sections.why: The comment on driverBasis says a pillar with too few lesson facts falls back to other evidence, which is recorded here.
sections.watch_out: A pillar on the descriptive fallback basis rests on weaker evidence than one built from lesson facts.

sections.name: patternSchema
sections.title: Pattern rules
sections.what: Describes a theme that runs across projects, marked as a success or a failure, with its detail and the evidence and projects behind it.
sections.why: Likely reason: a pattern spans several projects, so both evidence and project lists are kept.
sections.watch_out: The kind must be success or failure, so a neutral pattern will fail validation.

sections.name: recommendationSchema
sections.title: Recommendation rules
sections.what: Describes one recommendation: its text, the pillar it belongs to, and the evidence supporting it.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each recommendation traceable to its evidence.
sections.watch_out: The pillar can be empty, so code that groups recommendations by pillar must handle the missing case.

sections.name: slideBlockSchema
sections.title: Slide block rules
sections.what: Describes one slide: its title, optional subtitle, bullet points, footnotes, an optional chart with labels and values, and extra data used for splitting long slides.
sections.why: The comment says the extra data holds the boundaries used to split long pillar slides across pages.
sections.watch_out: The chart kind allows only three names, and the extra data is loosely typed, so mistakes there are not caught.

sections.name: recipeResultSchema, RecipeResult, RecipeFact, RecipePillar, SlideBlock
sections.title: Whole result rules and shorthand types
sections.what: Defines the full saved result: version, time, scope, methodology with sources, assessments, projects, facts, pillars, patterns, recommendations, slides and totals. Exports short names for the whole result, a fact, a pillar and a slide.
sections.why: Likely reason: one top-level rule lets the renderer read the result safely.
sections.watch_out: The name RecipeFact is also used in types.ts with a different shape, so check which file an import comes from.

sections.name: SHELL_SLIDE_IDS
sections.title: Standard slide names
sections.what: Lists the five standard framing slides (cover, executive summary, agenda, recipes overview, assessment matrix). Pillar slides are named by their pillar. An older name is kept as a marked alias.
sections.why: The comments say pillar slides are created dynamically, and the old name is marked deprecated.
sections.watch_out: Renaming any of these slides will break code that looks them up by name.

summary: Defines the validation rules for the saved Lessons Learnt result that the slide renderer reads, for the earlier V1 engines.
purpose: Gives one checked description of a result so the code that writes it and the slide renderer agree on fields and names.
why: The header says engines write this shape and the PowerPoint renderer reads only this, with the saved database summary as the source of truth. A reason for checking data with schemas is not stated in the code, but a likely reason is catching bad data early.
how: Lists the allowed outcome names, then defines a rule for each part of the result: honesty labels, facts, projects, sub-drivers, pillars, patterns, recommendations, slides and the whole result. It exports matching types for other code to use, and ends with a fixed list of standard slide names.
inputs: Data written by the older engines, which is checked against these rules when read.
outputs: Typed objects when the data is valid, and an error when it is not. Exports the types RecipeResult, RecipeFact, RecipePillar and SlideBlock.
risks: Must be kept in step with the engines and the renderer. A field added to one but not to this file may fail validation or be dropped. Several fields are optional for older runs.
debug: If a saved result fails to load, read the field named in the error and compare it with this file. Compare the honesty labels here with the verification labels in types.ts, since the two sets use different words, such as unconfirmed here and unverified there.
